evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Jules: 'This should take me about five to ten minutes and then I'll get you the estimate.' — framing present but no clear wait for customer affirmation; customer says 'Yup' but not in response to a direct yes/no ask.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Shannon Burke), move day (Wednesday 30th Sept), route (Dallas to Dallas, 2320 Taylor St to 3600 Wheeler St), size (700 sq ft one-bedroom). All four confirmed.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Jules: 'Can I have quick question aside from the quote itself, do you have any specific concerns about your upcoming move or any any important questions you want answers to when this call today?' Asked before probing. Greg responds with concern about what's included in quote and travel/fuel fees.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Jules follows up on Greg's concern about inclusions: 'Definitely that is something I can get for you and they think you're gonna like the structure of our pricing but I can discuss all of that a little bit later.' Later in the call, Jules addresses the concern in detail during the pricing section, covering hourly rate, what's included, no hidden fees, tools, wrapping, minimum/prorating. The concern was addressed substantively, constituting two-layer depth.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Jules acknowledges the concern ('Definitely that is something I can get for you') but never reflects back the customer's stated concern as a summary check.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment), floor (3rd floor origin, 5th floor destination), rooms (one bedroom), elevator status (stairs, not elevator), oversized items (bed disassembly, dresser, couch, coffee table, two-person dining set, boxes already packed), box count (estimated 15). Elevator status for origin was unconfirmed ('right now we're not sure if it's actually under the third floor') but customer committed to follow up. Seven items substantially covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. Jules does not ask 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' Everything is already boxed by customer.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: True. Jules: 'Do you know how many boxes she already has? ... Well usually for apartments this size, we see around fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think she's gonna be within that range?' Customer confirms 15.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full. Jules: 'for this move just to give you an idea of course it still depends on how much stuff she actually has for us to move but I think this move will just take anywhere from three to four hours, you know with an estimated cost of $612 to $2,816, should it take us four hours.' Range anchored ($612–$2,816), personalized to 3–4 hour window and apartment details (700 sq ft, one bedroom, 15 boxes, furniture list).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Jules discloses rate structure: '$204 per hour for two movers and one truck that our rate includes absolutely everything, you know the gas, the truck taxes and insurance.' Explains no hidden fees: 'we do not have any additional fees, you know, we don't have anything like a fuel fee, no disassemble, reassembly fees, no hidden fees of any type at all.' Explains minimum/prorating: 'we have a minimum of two and a half hours and then after that we prorate every fifteen minutes.' Commitment language present ('we do not have any additional fees').
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After pricing is disclosed, Jules says 'Does that make sense so for' and customer repeats back the math ('So you're saying so two and a half times 204'). No 'Does that feel fair?' framing, and no pause given for reflection — the conversation moves directly into confirmation.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: None. The On-Time Guarantee is never mentioned. Jules gives a time window ('12:30 to 2:30 in the afternoon') but does not explain the discount-if-late commitment.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: None. No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000, no deductible, built into rate) is never mentioned.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. No closing question like 'Does that put those to rest?' after the two promises would have been delivered. Since neither promise was delivered, there is no loop to close.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Jules moves directly to 'Would you like to get this scheduled for Wednesday right now?' with no final concerns probe like 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: With out. Jules: 'As well if you know right now we do have availability on Wednesday afternoon again we're going to be arriving around 12:30 AM to 2:30 PM would you like or help with the move?' Phrased as offer with implicit out (implies customer can decline). Later, after payment discussion, Jules does not re-ask; customer has already said 'Yes please' to scheduling.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False. No mention of rate lock or that the quoted price holds.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: Move date (Wednesday 30th Sept), unit numbers (2323-6 origin, 1520 destination), phone number on file (daughter's 972-940-1466, father's 469-939-4757 as backup), addresses (2320 Taylor St to 3600 Wheeler St). Missing: crew size (two movers + one truck mentioned in rate, but not explicitly confirmed for this booking), arrival window confirmed (12:30–2:30 PM), no notes documented about customer's stated concerns (quote inclusions, travel/fuel fees) for the crew.

top_strength: Jules systematically gathered all essential logistics details (property type, floor, room count, furniture, box count, both addresses) and delivered a specific, anchored price range ($612–$2,816 for 3–4 hours) personalized to this customer's 700-sq-ft one-bedroom move.
coaching_note: Critical gap: The Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) were never delivered — this is the highest-impact miss on the call. Additionally, no final concerns check was asked, and no 'Does that feel fair?' pause was given after pricing; add these three items to close the sale stronger.
